question: Can a bounded three-view reference/query memory expose complementary observations on consumed PV28 before testing whether memory aggregation repairs its frozen single-view zero-cycle failure?

partial_view_rules.selection: Use the already frozen anti-sliver partial-view admission. Greedily add the view exposing the most previously unseen depth-consistent target vertices; ties use larger short-side fraction, higher visible ratio, then earlier frame. Stop at three views or zero marginal gain.

next_decision: If both sides supply at least two complementary views, freeze the full bounded reference-by-query portfolio and run the unchanged coherent-cycle carrier once with every reference view against both fixed cross-family controls. Aggregate by any positive support but any negative false commit fails the memory gate.

literature_motivation.used_principle: Persist several complementary object observations as one instance memory instead of making downstream association depend on one privileged view.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the three-view budget, admission rules, greedy selection or family after observing the portfolio
use RGB/model outcomes to select memory members
change the existing carrier, controls or support thresholds during the memory test
claim consumed Development as fresh confirmation
claim_boundary: This is a geometry/depth-only posthoc source diagnostic on consumed PV28. It can establish only whether bounded complementary observations exist; it is not RGB/model evidence, exact-instance binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, benefit, reliability or safety.
